title: Chiasmal Compression & Pituitary Adenomas: The Neuro-Ophthalmic Blueprint
summary: A comprehensive review of the ophthalmic and endocrinological management of pituitary adenomas, focusing on the localization of bitemporal hemianopia and the clinical sequelae of hyperprolactinemia.

sections.title: Anatomical Pathophysiology: The Chiasmal Junction
sections.content: Pituitary adenomas arise from the sella turcica. As they grow superiorly, they compress the decussating fibers of the optic chiasm (the inferior nasal fibers). This results in the classic bitemporal hemianopia. If the tumor grows anteriorly, it compresses the optic nerves (causing central scotomas); if posteriorly, it compresses the optic tracts (causing homonymous hemianopia).

rows: Early detection due to menstrual cycle changes
Late presentation; often present with macroadenoma/visual loss

sections.title: Red Flags: Neuro-Ophthalmic Emergencies
content: Pituitary Apoplexy: Acute headache, nausea, ophthalmoplegia (CN III, IV, VI palsy).
Rapid visual field constriction: Impending chiasmal decompensation.
Signs of adrenal crisis: Hypotension, electrolyte imbalance.

content.explanation: Fields (Humphrey/Goldmann), Acuity (Snellen/ETDRS), Motility (CN 3,4,6 status), Endocrine (Hormone panel).

sections.title: Diagnostic Workflow
content: Step 2: OCT of Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer (RNFL) to assess ganglion cell loss.
Step 3: MRI Brain/Sella with and without Gadolinium contrast (Gold standard).
Step 5: Multidisciplinary team review (Neuro-Ophthalmology, Neurosurgery, Endocrinology).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Cabergoline is generally preferred over Bromocriptine due to better side-effect profile.
Always check serum prolactin even in non-secreting tumors to rule out 'Stalk Effect' (compression of dopamine-inhibiting pathways).
The 'Pituitary Stalk Effect' can cause modest prolactin elevations (typically <100-150 ng/mL).
Visual fields should be monitored post-operatively every 3-6 months in the first year.
